subject: lacewing larva
title: This Tiny Larva Knocks Out Six Termites Before It Takes a Bite

scenes.text: This larva kills termites without biting first.
It's a baby beaded lacewing, and it lives in rotting logs packed with termites.
It walks up to a termite and points its rear end at the termite's head.
Then it releases a chemical from its anus. Within one to three minutes, the termite stops moving.
One release can knock out up to six termites at once.
Only then does it bite. Death by fart, and it's real science.

description:
Larvae of the beaded lacewing Lomamyia latipennis live among termites in rotting wood. A 1981 study in Nature found they release a chemical from the anus that immobilises termites within about one to three minutes.
A single release can subdue up to six termites, which the larva then feeds on.
Which insect weapon is weirder than this one?
first_comment: Scientists actually named the chemical an allomone: a scent made to affect another species. What's the strangest way you've heard an animal hunt?
